title: Which digit is the thousandth, and where does the millionth digit sit?
description: The counting numbers are written one after another and the digits are counted group by group. The thousandth digit, the number holding the millionth digit and the place of the five thousandth five are all found by counting in groups.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the digits in groups by length of number, and stop when the total reaches the target. Watch for students who forget the left-over digits, which show where inside a number the target digit falls.

source: Figure it Out, Q6 (digits written one after the other)
video_script.why: The child can read and compare large numbers, and now counts the digits of the counting numbers in groups by length.
video_script.substitution: Count the digits group by group (one digit numbers, two digit numbers, and so on); divide what is left by the length of the next group; the left-over digits show the place inside the number.
video_script.anchor: the counting numbers written in one long row: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 1 0 1 1 1 2, with the tenth and eleventh digits marked
video_script.payoff_line: Count the digits group by group and stop when the total reaches the target

final_answer.spoken: the thousandth digit is three, in the number three hundred seventy

maths_rules: digits up to 99: 9 + 180 = 189; 1000 - 189 = 811; 811 / 3 = 270 remainder 1; the 271st three digit number is 100 + 270 = 370; its first digit is 3

fives: in 1 to 9999 each of 4 places holds 5 in 1000 numbers, so 4000; in each of 10,000 to 10,999, 11,000 to 11,999, 12,000 to 12,999 three places hold 5 in 100 numbers each, so 300 for each thousand, 900 in all; total 4900 by 12,999

from 13,000 each block of 100 numbers has 10 fives in the ones place and 10 in the tens place, so 20; 13,000 to 13,399 give 80; total 4980; the last 20 fives come in 13,400 to 13,495: 13405, 13415, 13425, 13435, 13445, 13450 to 13459 (13455 has two), 13465, 13475, 13485, 13495; the 20th is the ones digit of 13,495
video_script.design: One idea: count digits by groups and stop at the target. The long row of digits stays in the anchor band; the working band builds three counts one below another. The fives count is shown by hand grouping, not as a computer count. No hard clear.
open_questions: The book answer key gives 13,995 for the fives question; the worklist and a direct count give 13,495. The video follows 13,495 and shows the hand grouping.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 to 9 use 9 digits; 10 to 99 use 90 x 2 = 180; so 189 digits; 1000 - 189 = 811; 811 / 3 = 270, 1 left over; the 271st 3 digit number is 100 + 270 = 370; its first digit is 3

marks.m1b: 9 and 180 appear and are added to 189
marks.m4: 370 is lit and its first digit 3 is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the thousandth digit.
<bookmark mark='m1b'/>Numbers one to nine use nine digits, and ten to ninety nine use one hundred eighty.
That makes one hundred eighty nine digits.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One thousand less one hundred eighty nine leaves eight hundred eleven digits.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eight hundred eleven divided by three gives two hundred seventy numbers and one digit left over.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>That digit is the first digit of the next number, three hundred seventy.

marks.m1: the heading the millionth digit appears
marks.m5: 1,85,185 is lit and its first digit 1 is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the millionth digit.
Three digit numbers use two thousand seven hundred digits.
<bookmark mark='m1b'/>Four digit numbers use thirty six thousand, and five digit numbers use four lakh fifty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Numbers up to five digits use four lakh eighty eight thousand eight hundred eighty nine digits.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ten lakh less that total leaves five lakh eleven thousand one hundred eleven digits.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Dividing by six gives eighty five thousand one hundred eighty five numbers and one digit left over.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>That digit starts the next number, one lakh eighty five thousand one hundred eighty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: up to 9999, each of 4 places has 5 in 1000 numbers: 4000 fives; each thousand from 10,000 to 12,999: 3 x 100 = 300, so 900; total 4900; 100 more needed; 13,000 to 13,399: 4 x 20 = 80; 13,400 to 13,495: the last 20, ending at 13,495

marks.m4b: the four blocks up to 13,399 are lit
marks.m5: 13,400 to 13,495 is lit with its twenty fives counted

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, count the fives.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Up to nine thousand nine hundred ninety nine, each of four places shows a five one thousand times.
That makes four thousand fives.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The next three thousands, up to twelve thousand nine hundred ninety nine, give three hundred fives each.
That brings the total to four thousand nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>One hundred more are needed, and every block of one hundred numbers from thirteen thousand holds twenty.
<bookmark mark='m4b'/>Four blocks, up to thirteen thousand three hundred ninety nine, give eighty.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>The last twenty fives come as we count up from thirteen thousand four hundred.
The twentieth is in thirteen thousand four hundred ninety five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: 270 x 3 + 189 = 999 digits, so digit 1000 starts 370; 85,185 x 6 + 4,88,889 = 9,99,999 digits, so the millionth digit starts 1,85,185
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, the checks.
<bookmark mark='m1b'/>Two hundred seventy numbers of three digits, plus one hundred eighty nine, make nine hundred ninety nine digits.
The next digit, the thousandth, starts three hundred seventy.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The same check for the millionth digit gives nine lakh ninety nine thousand nine hundred ninety nine digits.
<bookmark mark='m2b'/>The next digit starts one lakh eighty five thousand one hundred eighty five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the 1000th digit is 3, in 370; the millionth digit is 1, in 1,85,185; the 5000th five is written in 13,495
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Count the digits group by group and stop when the total reaches the target.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The thousandth digit is three, in the number three hundred seventy.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The millionth digit is one, in the number one lakh eighty five thousand one hundred eighty five.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The five thousandth five is written in thirteen thousand four hundred ninety five.
